strings.title: Discord webhook URL
strings.desc: A Discord webhook is the most common way to send stolen data (tokens, passwords, IP) to the attacker.

strings.title: Telegram bot API
strings.desc: Sends data through a Telegram bot – a popular exfiltration channel for stealers.

strings.title: Request catcher / exfil service
strings.desc: Services like webhook.site or pipedream collect arbitrary HTTP requests – no legit mod needs that.

strings.title: Loads content from paste sites
strings.desc: Raw paste links are often used to fetch the real webhook URL or payload without changing the JAR.

strings.title: Tunnel / dynamic DNS domain
strings.desc: ngrok, DuckDNS, No-IP and co. hide the attacker's server behind changing addresses.

strings.title: Anonymous file host
strings.desc: Anonymous file hosts are used to deliver second-stage malware or upload stolen data.

strings.title: Discord CDN file link
strings.desc: Downloading executables from Discord attachments is a typical loader pattern.

strings.title: URL with a hard-coded IP address
strings.desc: Connecting to a fixed IP instead of a domain is typical for C2 servers.

strings.title: Looks up your public IP
strings.desc: Queries your public IP – a classic part of IP grabbers.

strings.title: Accesses browser passwords/cookies
strings.desc: Paths to 'Login Data', 'Local State' or Firefox key files are only needed by password stealers.

strings.title: Browser profile folders
strings.desc: References browser profile folders (Chrome, Brave, Opera, Edge, Firefox …).

strings.title: Accesses Discord token storage
strings.desc: Discord tokens live in 'Local Storage/leveldb'. A mod has no business there.

strings.title: Regex for finding Discord tokens
strings.desc: This pattern searches files for Discord tokens – a clear sign of a token grabber.

strings.title: Accesses launcher accounts
strings.desc: Reads account/token files of other launchers (Vanilla, Lunar, Feather, Essential, TLauncher, Prism …).

strings.title: Accesses crypto wallets
strings.desc: Paths/IDs of crypto wallets (Exodus, Electrum, MetaMask, Phantom …) – the target of wallet stealers.

strings.title: Accesses Telegram session data
strings.desc: The 'tdata' folder contains the Telegram Desktop session.

strings.title: Accesses Steam login data
strings.desc: ssfn files and loginusers.vdf allow taking over Steam accounts.

strings.title: Accesses credentials of other programs
strings.desc: FileZilla, VPN profiles, SSH keys, AWS credentials, authenticator data …

strings.title: Crypto address pattern
strings.desc: Regex for Bitcoin/Ethereum/Monero addresses – the basis of a clipboard hijacker that swaps copied addresses.

strings.title: Hard-coded crypto address
strings.desc: A built-in wallet address – in clippers, the attacker's address.

strings.title: Windows autostart persistence
strings.desc: Startup folder, Run registry keys or scheduled tasks – the malware restarts with every Windows boot, even without Minecraft.

strings.title: Linux/macOS autostart persistence
strings.desc: LaunchAgents, crontab, systemd or shell rc files – the program restarts automatically.

strings.title: Disables antivirus/Defender
strings.desc: Adds Defender exclusions or disables real-time protection – clearly malicious.
strings.re: Add-MpPreference|Set-MpPreference|ExclusionPath|ExclusionProcess|DisableRealtimeMonitoring|DisableBehaviorMonitoring|DisableAntiSpyware|DisableIOAVProtection|vssadmin.{0,20}delete|bcdedit|wevtutil cl|netsh advfirewall set|sc stop WinDefend|Windows Defender[\\/]{1,2}Exclusions

strings.title: Shell download command (LOLBin)
strings.desc: PowerShell/certutil/bitsadmin commands that download and run code.

strings.title: Calls PowerShell/script hosts
strings.desc: Starts powershell, wscript, cscript or mshta.

strings.title: Executable file name
strings.desc: References .exe/.dll/.bat/.ps1/.vbs – often the target of a dropper.

strings.title: Crypto miner
strings.desc: Mining pool addresses or XMRig parameters – your PC is secretly used for mining.

strings.title: Anti-VM / anti-analysis
strings.desc: Looks for VirtualBox, sandboxes, debuggers or reverse-engineering tools to hide from analysis.

strings.title: /pay or trade command in code
strings.desc: The code contains a money/trade command. Combined with automatic chat sending this is a classic 'auto-pay' stealer that sends your in-game money to the author.

strings.title: Hard-coded /pay command with a target
strings.desc: A /pay command with a fixed recipient and/or amount – sends your money to a specific player.

strings.title: Operator/permission command in code
strings.desc: Commands like /op, LuckPerms or PEX permission grants.
strings.re: ^/?(minecraft:)?(op|deop) [A-Za-z0-9_%{}$]|^/?(op|deop) $|^/?lp user .{1,40} (permission set|parent (add|set))|^/?luckperms user|^/?pex user .{1,40} (add|group set)|^/?(manuadd|mangadd) |^/?gamemode (creative|1) |^/?whitelist add |^/?(minecraft:)?op$

strings.title: Blockchain used as C2 address book (EtherHiding)
strings.desc: Queries a smart contract on Polygon/Ethereum/BSC via eth_call. Malware like SilentNet stores its current server address there so the server can never be taken down. No normal mod talks to a blockchain.

strings.title: DNS-over-HTTPS
strings.desc: Resolves domains itself over HTTPS (Cloudflare/Google DoH), bypassing DNS blocks and Pi-hole – typical for malware hiding its server.

strings.title: Starts a bundled Python runtime
strings.desc: Downloads or unpacks a portable Python environment and runs a script – Minecraft mods do not need Python. A classic way to load a stealer.

strings.title: Stealer wording in code
strings.desc: The code refers to itself as a stealer/grabber.

strings.title: Reads the access token via reflection
strings.desc: Method/field names of the Minecraft session token appear as text in the code, so the token is read via reflection – a trick to dodge scanners that only check direct calls.

strings.title: Builds JSON containing accessToken
strings.desc: A JSON object with an accessToken field is built – usually to send the token somewhere.

strings.title: Installs a Windows service or WMI trigger
strings.desc: Creates a Windows service, an installer service or a WMI event subscription – the program runs again on every boot, often with SYSTEM rights, and survives uninstalling the mod.

strings.title: Hooks into every Java program (JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS)
strings.desc: Touches JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS / _JAVA_OPTIONS or adds a -javaagent. If it sets them, every Java program you start (Minecraft, launchers, other games) loads the malware again.

strings.title: Targets the Discord client files
strings.desc: Refers to discord_desktop_core / index.js or app.asar. Token stealers patch these files so they get your new token after every password change – even after the mod is deleted.

strings.title: Touches other launchers or clients
strings.desc: Refers to folders of other launchers/clients (Lunar, Feather, Prism, MultiMC, TLauncher) or launcher JVM arguments. Malware uses this to infect other installs or to add itself to their start arguments.

strings.title: UAC bypass (silent admin rights)
strings.desc: Uses a known trick (fodhelper, ComputerDefaults, eventvwr, sdclt, ms-settings handler, cmstp) to get administrator rights without the Windows prompt.

strings.title: Asks for administrator rights
strings.desc: Starts something with 'Run as administrator'. A Minecraft mod never needs admin rights.

strings.title: Changes firewall rules
strings.desc: Adds or disables Windows firewall rules – opens your PC for incoming connections (backdoor) or blocks security updates.

strings.title: Changes the system proxy
strings.desc: Sets a system-wide proxy – all your browser traffic can be routed through the attacker (man-in-the-middle).

strings.title: Installs a root certificate
strings.desc: Adds a trusted root certificate. With it the attacker can read and change your HTTPS traffic, including logins.

strings.title: Accesses the hosts file
strings.desc: The hosts file decides where domain names point. Malware edits it to block antivirus updates or redirect sites to fake pages.

strings.title: Deletes backups / shadow copies
strings.desc: Deletes Windows shadow copies, backups or recovery – done by ransomware right before encrypting your files.

strings.title: Hides files
strings.desc: Marks files as hidden/system so you do not see them in Explorer – typical for installed malware.

strings.title: Deletes itself after running
strings.desc: Runs a delayed delete command on its own file – the dropper removes its traces after installing the real malware.

strings.title: Kills other programs
strings.desc: Ends other processes (taskkill / Stop-Process) – used to close Discord or browsers before stealing their files, or to kill antivirus.

strings.title: Tor network / Tor bridges
strings.desc: Uses Tor (.onion addresses, Tor bridges like obfs4/snowflake/meek). The attacker's server is hidden and cannot be traced or taken down.

strings.title: Tunnel / port forwarding
strings.desc: Opens a tunnel or forwards a router port (frp, chisel, bore, localtonet, serveo, UPnP AddPortMapping). Your PC becomes reachable from the internet – the base of a backdoor or proxy bridge.

strings.title: Receives commands from a Telegram bot
strings.desc: Polls a Telegram bot for new messages (getUpdates) – the attacker sends commands to your PC through Telegram.

strings.title: Connects to Discord as a bot
strings.desc: Logs into the Discord gateway or reads channel messages. Chat-bridge mods do this legitimately; RATs use it to receive commands. Check what the messages trigger.

strings.title: Remote-access tool wording
strings.desc: Contains phrases from remote-access tools (reverse shell, hidden VNC, back-connect, botnet).

EXEC.label: Starts processes
EXEC.title: Starts external programs
EXEC.desc: Uses Runtime.exec / ProcessBuilder, so it can run any command on your PC.

SOCKET.label: Raw sockets
SOCKET.title: Opens raw socket connections
SOCKET.desc: Opens TCP/UDP connections without HTTP – typical for C2 channels, but also used by proxies or voice chat.

SERVER_SOCKET.label: Listens on ports
SERVER_SOCKET.title: Opens a local server port
SERVER_SOCKET.desc: Starts a server socket. Can be abused for remote access (backdoor).

CLASSLOAD.label: URLClassLoader
CLASSLOAD.title: Creates its own class loaders
CLASSLOAD.desc: Creates a URLClassLoader, which can load foreign JARs or classes at runtime.

DEFINE_CLASS.label: Defines classes from bytes
DEFINE_CLASS.title: Defines classes directly from bytes
DEFINE_CLASS.desc: Calls defineClass – code is created from a byte array that is not a normal class in the JAR.

NATIVE.label: Native libraries
NATIVE.title: Loads native libraries
NATIVE.desc: System.load/loadLibrary or JNA – native code runs outside the Java sandbox.

DPAPI.label: Windows DPAPI
DPAPI.title: Decrypts protected Windows data (DPAPI)
DPAPI.desc: CryptUnprotectData is almost only used to decrypt saved browser passwords and cookies.

SCREEN.label: Screen capture
SCREEN.title: Takes screenshots of the desktop
SCREEN.desc: java.awt.Robot.createScreenCapture captures the whole screen (not just the game).

KEYHOOK.label: Global keyboard hook
KEYHOOK.title: Global keyboard/mouse hook (JNativeHook)
KEYHOOK.desc: Registers system-wide keyboard events – even outside Minecraft. Classic keylogger tool.

INSTRUMENT.label: Java instrumentation
INSTRUMENT.title: Uses Java instrumentation
INSTRUMENT.desc: Can modify loaded classes at runtime.

ATTACH.label: Attaches to other JVMs
ATTACH.title: Attaches to other Java processes
ATTACH.desc: VirtualMachine.attach injects agents into other Java processes.

MC_TOKEN.label: Minecraft access token
MC_TOKEN.title: Reads the Minecraft access token
MC_TOKEN.desc: The session token lets anyone log in as you without a password. Normal mods almost never need it.

BUKKIT_OP.label: setOp()
BUKKIT_OP.title: Grants operator rights (setOp)
BUKKIT_OP.desc: The plugin can give players OP. Legit for admin plugins, but the core of almost every force-OP backdoor.

BUKKIT_PERM.label: Permission attachments
BUKKIT_PERM.title: Sets permissions directly
BUKKIT_PERM.desc: Creates PermissionAttachments – can silently give players permissions.

WEBCAM.label: Webcam
WEBCAM.title: Accesses the webcam
WEBCAM.desc: Uses a webcam library (webcam-capture, JavaCV, OpenCV VideoCapture). A Minecraft mod has no reason to turn on your camera.

combos.title: Session token stealer
combos.desc: Reads the Minecraft access token and sends data to a webhook/exfil service. The attacker can take over your account with it.

combos.title: Session token stealer
combos.desc: Reads the Minecraft access token and sends data to a webhook/exfil service. The attacker can take over your account with it.

combos.title: Access token + network
combos.desc: The same class reads the Minecraft access token and opens a network connection.

combos.title: Data stealer with upload
combos.desc: Accesses passwords/tokens/wallets of other programs and has a way to send them out.

combos.title: Browser password stealer
combos.desc: Combines DPAPI decryption with browser/credential paths – decrypts saved passwords and cookies.

combos.title: Downloads code from the internet and runs it
combos.desc: Loads bytes over the network and defines classes from them – the real malware is not in the JAR and can be swapped at any time.

combos.title: Loads classes from a remote source
combos.desc: A URLClassLoader combined with network access or suspicious download addresses (stage-2 loader).

combos.title: Decrypts hidden code in memory
combos.desc: Base64/encryption plus defineClass: hidden code is unpacked and loaded only at runtime.

combos.title: Dropper: download + save + execute
combos.desc: Downloads a file, saves it and runs it or loads it as code. Classic behaviour of second-stage malware.

combos.title: Network + process start
combos.desc: The same class talks to the internet and starts external programs.

combos.title: Downloads executable files
combos.desc: Download and save together with .exe/.dll/.bat/.ps1 file names.

combos.title: Installs extra JARs into mods/plugins
combos.desc: Downloads JAR files into the mods/plugins folder. Legit auto-updaters do this too – check the download address carefully.

combos.title: Modifies other JAR files
combos.desc: Reads JARs and writes new JAR/ZIP files – how worm infectors like fractureiser spread to other mods.

combos.title: Infects mods/plugins (worm)
combos.desc: Searches the mods/plugins folder and rewrites JAR files – spreads to all your other mods.

combos.title: Clipboard hijacker (clipper)
combos.desc: Reads/replaces the clipboard and knows crypto address patterns – copied wallet addresses get swapped for the attacker's.

combos.title: Screenshots with upload
combos.desc: Captures your desktop and has an upload channel.

combos.title: Keylogger
combos.desc: Global keyboard hook with a way to save or upload keystrokes.

combos.title: Force-OP backdoor
combos.desc: Reads chat messages and grants OP – a secret chat password gives the attacker full server rights.

combos.title: Chat-controlled console commands
combos.desc: Chat messages trigger console commands with permission commands.

combos.title: Chat events + console commands
combos.desc: The same class reads chat messages and runs commands as console – check for a hidden trigger.

combos.title: OP for a hard-coded UUID
combos.desc: setOp combined with a built-in player UUID.

combos.title: Economy manipulation for fixed players
combos.desc: Vault economy access together with hard-coded UUIDs or chat triggers.

combos.title: Auto-/pay stealer
combos.desc: Sends /pay or trade commands from your account on its own – your in-game money ends up with the attacker.

combos.title: Sends OP/permission commands
combos.desc: Runs /op or permission commands automatically.

combos.title: System/IP info sent to webhook
combos.desc: Collects PC name, user name, HWID or IP and has a webhook/exfil channel.

combos.title: Remote shell / backdoor
combos.desc: Socket connection combined with process execution – the attacker can run commands on your PC.

combos.title: Sets up autostart
combos.desc: Autostart paths/commands together with process start or file writes.

combos.title: Encrypted container + class loader
combos.desc: The JAR contains encrypted data blobs and code that defines classes from bytes – typical for packed malware.

combos.title: Disguised classes get loaded
combos.desc: Class files are disguised as resources and the JAR contains its own class loading code.

combos.title: Relaunches itself as a separate Java process
combos.desc: Finds the path of its own JAR and starts it with java/javaw as a separate process. The code keeps running independently of Minecraft – even after you close the game.

combos.title: Hidden background process
combos.desc: Starts a Java process whose output goes to NUL or that is marked 'restarted/detached'. Malware keeps running invisibly this way (known from SilentNet).

combos.title: Hand-made HTTP client over raw sockets
combos.desc: Writes HTTP requests by hand over Socket/SSLSocket instead of using Java's HTTP classes, dodging scanners that look for URL/HttpClient.

combos.title: Blockchain-controlled C2 server
combos.desc: Reads its server address from a blockchain and has a network channel – the attacker's server is practically impossible to take down.

combos.title: Unpacks a payload and runs it
combos.desc: Unpacks archives to disk and then starts a process – second-stage malware is being deployed.

combos.title: Session token stealer
combos.desc: Reads the Minecraft access token and has a hidden network channel (raw sockets/blockchain C2).

combos.title: Remote desktop / hidden VNC
combos.desc: Captures the screen and moves your mouse/keyboard, with a network channel – the attacker can watch and control your PC.

combos.title: Remote-controlled through a bot
combos.desc: Receives commands via a Telegram/Discord bot and can run programs, take screenshots or load code – a remote-access trojan.

combos.title: Runs scripts from the network
combos.desc: A script engine (JavaScript/Groovy) together with network access – code can be sent from a server and run on your PC.

combos.title: Microphone recording with upload
combos.desc: Records the microphone and has a webhook/bot channel to send it out.

combos.title: PC exposed through a tunnel
combos.desc: Opens a tunnel/port forward or uses Tor and can run commands or accept connections – a backdoor reachable from the internet.

combos.title: UAC bypass with process start
combos.desc: Bypasses the admin prompt and starts a program – it then runs with full administrator rights.

combos.title: Changes security settings via commands
combos.desc: Runs commands that change firewall, proxy, certificates or backups.

combos.title: Injects code into Discord
combos.desc: Writes files and targets Discord's core module – the classic Discord token-stealer injection that survives password changes.

combos.title: Modifies other launchers/clients
combos.desc: Writes into other launcher folders together with JAR files or start arguments – spreads to other Minecraft installs.

combos.title: Writes an autostart registry key
combos.desc: Writes the Windows registry together with autostart keys – starts again with Windows.

combos.title: Hides OP changes from the log
combos.desc: Filters the server log and can give OP – a backdoor that hides its traces from admins.

combos.title: Hides process starts from the log
combos.desc: Filters log output and starts external programs.

combos.title: Downloads and loads plugins
combos.desc: Loads plugins at runtime and has network access – extra plugins can be installed on the server without the admin knowing.

combos.title: Kills security or analysis tools
combos.desc: Ends processes and looks for antivirus/analysis tools.

combos.title: Interactive remote shell
combos.desc: Starts cmd/sh and connects it to a network connection – the attacker types commands on your PC.

families.name: fractureiser
families.desc: Worm from 2023 that spread through infected CurseForge/Bukkit projects, infected mods/plugins on the PC, stole browser/Discord/Minecraft data and set up persistence.

families.name: SilentNet
families.desc: SilentNet (silentnet.st) is a Minecraft RAT kit. Its loader gets injected into real mods, steals the Minecraft session token, fetches its server address from a blockchain (Polygon), downloads a hidden Python runtime and starts a stealer in the background.
